title: Moving charges in fields
examples: What is the relationship between the magnetic force and the velocity of a charge?
How does the magnetic field strength affect the radius of the path?
Can you explain the principle behind the cyclotron device?

explain.say: Today we explore the force on moving charges in magnetic fields. This is called the Lorentz force.
The force depends on the charge, the speed, and the strength of the field. The angle between them matters too.
When the charge moves perpendicular to the field, the force is at its maximum value. This means the sine is one.

items: Maximum force occurs when v is perpendicular to B.
In this case, sin(θ) equals one.

explain.say: If the charge moves in a circle, the magnetic force provides the centripetal force. This keeps it moving in a circle.
Equating these forces lets us find the radius of the circular path. The radius is proportional to the momentum.
The cyclotron uses a constant magnetic field to accelerate charged particles in a circle. It keeps them moving efficiently.

faq.q: What is the direction of the Lorentz force?
faq.a: You use the right-hand rule to find the direction. Point your fingers in the direction of velocity and curl them into the magnetic field. Your thumb points the force direction.
asks: How do I find the direction of the force?
What rule tells me the force direction?

faq.q: Does the magnetic force change the speed of the particle?
faq.a: No, the magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity. Because the force does no work, it only changes the direction, not the speed.
asks: Will the particle speed up or slow down?
Is the magnetic force doing work on the charge?

faq.q: What happens if the velocity is parallel to the field?
faq.a: If the velocity is parallel to the field, the angle is zero degrees. The sine of zero is zero, so the magnetic force becomes zero.
asks: If v is parallel to B, what is F?
When is the magnetic force zero?

faq.q: How does the radius change if I double the magnetic field?
faq.a: The radius is inversely proportional to the magnetic field strength. If you double the field, the radius will be halved.
asks: If B increases, does r increase or decrease?
What is the relationship between r and B?

faq.q: What is the main function of a cyclotron?
faq.a: A cyclotron accelerates charged particles by using a constant magnetic field. It uses alternating voltage to increase the particle's energy.
asks: How does a cyclotron work generally?

facts: The Lorentz force is given by the equation F = q(v x B).
If the velocity is perpendicular to the magnetic field, the force is maximum.
The magnetic force only changes the direction of motion, not the speed.
The radius of the path is given by r = mv / (qB) when v is perpendicular to B.

quiz.say: A proton moves perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. If the magnetic field strength is doubled, what happens to the radius of its circular path?
quiz.why: The radius formula shows it is inversely proportional to B, so doubling B halves r.

wrong.0: This confuses the relationship with direct proportionality.
wrong.1: The radius clearly depends on the magnetic field strength.
wrong.2: This suggests a squared relationship that is not present here.

quiz.say: If a particle moves parallel to the magnetic field, what is the resulting magnetic force?

options.show: The force is proportional to v squared.
options.say: The force is proportional to v squared.

quiz.why: When v is parallel to B, the angle is zero, making sin(0) zero.

wrong.0: The force depends linearly on velocity, not velocity squared.
wrong.1: Maximum force requires the velocity to be perpendicular to the field.
wrong.3: This only happens when the motion is perpendicular to the field.

quiz.say: In a cyclotron, what is the primary role of the alternating voltage?

options.show: It maintains the magnetic field strength.
options.say: It maintains the magnetic field strength.

options.show: It determines the radius of the path.
options.say: It determines the radius of the path.

options.show: It keeps the particles moving in a straight line.
options.say: It keeps the particles moving in a straight line.

options.show: It provides the energy to increase the particle's speed.
options.say: It provides the energy to increase the particle's speed.

quiz.why: The alternating voltage ensures the particle gains energy to maintain its circular path.

wrong.0: The magnetic field strength is provided by external magnets.
wrong.1: The radius is determined by the balance of magnetic and centripetal forces.
wrong.2: The magnetic field forces them into a circular path.
